sources.title: Excel VBA reference
sources.summary: Entry point for Excel concepts, the Excel object model and the separate Graph Visual Basic reference.

sources.title: Excel object model
sources.summary: Navigation entry for objects, methods, properties, events and enumerations. This landing page is not an inventory of every member.

sources.title: Excel Graph Visual Basic reference
sources.summary: Separate Graph object-model documentation, not Microsoft Graph REST and not an algorithmic dependency graph.

sources.title: VBA language reference
sources.summary: Connects language concepts, Microsoft Forms, how-to guidance, language members, definitions, editor add-in model and VBE UI help.

sources.title: Office library reference
sources.summary: Entry to Office-wide library concepts and object-model reference.

sources.title: VBA-Docs repository
sources.summary: Public Microsoft documentation repository with Language, Library-Reference, api and Excel concept branches. Includes documentation and code licenses.

sources.title: VBA-Docs publishing configuration
sources.summary: DocFX includes Markdown and YAML, excludes include files and license files from article publishing, and assigns metadata by paths. Path inference must still distinguish publishing redirects and case.

sources.title: VBA-Docs documentation license
sources.summary: CC BY 4.0 license: preserve attribution and notices, identify changes, and provide the license link. No endorsement is granted.

sources.title: VBA-Docs code license
sources.summary: Microsoft code license is MIT; retain copyright and permission notice when redistributing covered code.

sources.title: VS Code Agent Skills
sources.summary: Personal skills may be placed in ~/.copilot/skills/. Instructions are loaded on demand. Discovery does not guarantee invocation; support depends on the agent harness.

sources.title: Workbooks.Open
sources.summary: Returns the opened Workbook. Explicitly choose link updates and read-only mode. Programmatic opening requires an explicit macro-security policy.

sources.title: Application.AutomationSecurity
sources.summary: ForceDisable controls macros in programmatically opened files but does not disable Excel 4.0 macros. DisplayAlerts does not suppress security warnings. Capture and restore the prior security state.

sources.title: Worksheet.Change
sources.summary: Target can contain multiple cells. Recalculation changes do not trigger this event; use Calculate for recalculation-specific work.

sources.title: Range.Find
sources.summary: Returns Nothing when no match exists. Several search options persist between calls and the Find dialog; specify them explicitly. Handle wraparound in repeated searches.

sources.title: Range.Value2
sources.summary: Value2 does not use the Currency or Date subtypes; those values can be exposed as Double. It is not a formatting or locale parser.

sources.title: Range.Value
sources.summary: Multi-cell first-area reads return a two-dimensional Variant array. Multi-area array assignment is not properly supported. Size the destination to the array.

sources.title: Application.ThisWorkbook
sources.summary: Identifies the workbook containing the running macro. It is not an external COM-client workbook selector. Add-in code and the active user workbook may differ.

sources.title: Application.ActiveWorkbook
sources.summary: Identifies the workbook in the active window and can be Nothing. Protected View has separate access semantics.

sources.title: Range.Formula2
sources.summary: Uses array-evaluation semantics and may spill. Formula remains for backward compatibility. Confirm the target Excel supports dynamic arrays.

sources.title: ListObject.DataBodyRange
sources.summary: Identifies the table data range excluding its header. The skill additionally requires a defensive Nothing check for empty-table workflows.

sources.title: Application.DisplayAlerts
sources.summary: Suppresses selected prompts, not security. SaveAs may overwrite without confirmation. Cross-process callers must restore state explicitly.

sources.title: On Error statement
sources.summary: Distinguish enabled from actively handling error handlers. An error inside an active handler propagates to its caller. Resume Next must have a narrow justified scope.

sources.title: Resume statement
sources.summary: Resume retries the failing statement, Resume Next continues after it, and Resume label resumes at a local label. It requires an active error context.

sources.title: Debug.Assert
sources.summary: Suspends execution when its expression is False. The whole boolean expression is evaluated; do not use it instead of production validation.

sources.title: Debug menu
sources.summary: Describes Compile, watch commands, breakpoints and stepping. Compile is a VBE operation, not equivalent to a text linter.

sources.title: Debug toolbar
sources.summary: Provides Run, Break, Reset, stepping and diagnostic windows. Reset clears the stack and module state.

sources.title: Set and clear a breakpoint
sources.summary: Use F9 to stop at a statement and Ctrl+Shift+F9 to clear all breakpoints. Breakpoints are not persisted with saved code.

sources.title: Stop code execution
sources.summary: Distinguishes break mode from Reset and describes runtime errors, Stop, End and watch-triggered breaks.

sources.title: Trace code execution
sources.summary: Step Into enters callees; Step Over executes the call; Step Out completes the current procedure; Run to Cursor continues to a chosen statement.

sources.title: Use the Immediate window
sources.summary: Ctrl+G opens Immediate. Commands execute in a module context and can mutate state; inspect values before using assignments or procedure calls.

sources.title: Elements of run-time error handling (Access)
sources.summary: Supplementary explanation of error-handling flow. Transfer only language-level ideas; Access-specific object behavior is not an Excel contract.

sources.title: Add a watch expression
sources.summary: Define a watch and choose the narrowest relevant procedure/module context. Broad evaluation can slow execution.

sources.title: Edit a watch expression
sources.summary: Edit the expression, scope and watch type in the Watch window.

sources.title: Delete a watch expression
sources.summary: Remove an obsolete watch from the Watch window.

sources.title: Use Quick Watch
sources.summary: Inspect a selected expression in break mode using Shift+F9 and optionally promote it to a watch.

sources.title: UserForm object
sources.summary: UserForms represent loaded dialog instances. Multiple explicit instances may be created; controls are exposed through Controls.

sources.title: Initialize event
sources.summary: Occurs after loading an object and before it is shown; use for initial preparation rather than repeated business actions.

sources.title: Activate and Deactivate events
sources.summary: Activation concerns visible active windows within the application. It is not a one-time constructor, and unloading does not produce Deactivate.

sources.title: QueryClose event
sources.summary: CloseMode identifies control-menu close, code unload and other close causes. Cancel can prevent closing; avoid blocking application shutdown accidentally.

sources.title: Hide method
sources.summary: Hides without unloading; hidden controls remain accessible programmatically. Hiding an unloaded form can load it.

sources.title: Unload statement
sources.summary: Unloads the form. Read a modal dialog result before unloading, rather than re-accessing a default instance afterward.

sources.title: Show method
sources.summary: Supports modal and modeless display. Show loads an unloaded form. Code after modeless Show continues immediately.

sources.title: Add method (Microsoft Forms)
sources.summary: Adds tabs/pages or creates controls with a registered ProgID. Event wiring and ownership are separate engineering responsibilities.

sources.title: Controls collection
sources.summary: Access controls by their names or zero-based collection indexes; enumerate each relevant container instead of equating index with tab order.

sources.title: TabIndex property
sources.summary: Defines tab order, starting at zero. Verify focus order in the real form and its containers.

sources.title: MultiPage control
sources.summary: Hosts a Pages collection; Value identifies the active page. Use distinct pages for groups of controls.

sources.title: TabStrip control
sources.summary: Hosts Tabs and exposes SelectedItem. Switching a tab can select different data for shared controls; it is not a MultiPage replacement by name alone.

sources.title: 64-bit VBA overview
sources.summary: PtrSafe alone does not fix truncated handles. Use LongPtr for pointers/handles and review UDTs and assignments; Long remains 32-bit.

sources.title: Excel performance obstructions
sources.summary: Reduce unnecessary UI updates and worksheet/VBA transfers. Capture original application settings and restore them after work. Measure actual workloads.

sources.title: ChartObjects.Add
sources.summary: Creates an embedded ChartObject. Position and dimensions use points, not pixels.

sources.title: Chart.SetSourceData
sources.summary: Sets chart source from an explicit Range with optional row/column plotting orientation.

sources.title: SeriesCollection.NewSeries
sources.summary: Creates a Series for supported charts; it is not available for PivotChart reports.

sources.title: Chart.Export
sources.summary: Exports using an installed graphic filter and returns Boolean. Check both result and the expected file instead of assuming export succeeded.

sources.title: Workbook.RefreshAll
sources.summary: Refresh may run in the background. The current page also warns that a failing Power Query table refresh can leave old data without RefreshAll raising a runtime error.

sources.title: QueryTable.Refresh
sources.summary: Refreshes external data; BackgroundQuery=False makes supported SQL-query refresh synchronous. Missing connection details can produce dialogs or failures.

sources.title: PivotCaches.Create
sources.summary: Creates a PivotCache from a supported source type. Explicit source strings/names can avoid unexpected type-mismatch issues. xlPivotTableVersionCurrent is not accepted.

sources.title: Application.Quit
sources.summary: Quits Excel. Unsaved workbooks may prompt; suppressing alerts may discard them. Quit only the instance owned by the current operation.

sources.title: Application.EnableEvents
sources.summary: Controls Excel application events. Preserve the previous value; do not assume it was True on entry.

sources.title: Workbook.SaveCopyAs
sources.summary: Writes a copy without changing the open workbook in memory. It does not itself create a transactional rollback strategy.

sources.title: Option Explicit statement
sources.summary: Requires variable declarations and surfaces undeclared names at compile time. It does not replace explicit typing or business validation.

sources.title: IIf function
sources.summary: Evaluates both result expressions. Use an If block when a branch could fail or have side effects.

sources.title: Dim statement
sources.summary: Declares variables and arrays. WithEvents belongs in class modules, cannot form an array and cannot be combined with New.

sources.title: Sub statement
sources.summary: Declares procedures and parameters. VBA defaults to ByRef, unlike VB.NET. Specify parameter intent explicitly.

sources.title: DoEvents function
sources.summary: Yields to the operating system to process queued events. Guard against re-entry; it does not turn VBA into a background worker.

sources.title: Data type summary
sources.summary: Summarizes VBA storage and ranges: Integer is 16-bit, Long 32-bit, Currency is scaled integer, and Double uses floating point.

sources.title: Collection object
sources.summary: Ordered group with Add, Item, Remove and Count. Do not assume it offers Dictionary.Exists.

sources.title: Dictionary object
sources.summary: Key/item container with Exists, Keys, Items and CompareMode. Availability of the scripting component is a deployment dependency.

sources.title: GetActiveWindow (Win32)
sources.summary: Returns an HWND for the calling thread or NULL, not necessarily the foreground window of another process.

sources.title: Sleep (Win32)
sources.summary: Suspends the current thread; its milliseconds parameter is DWORD, not a pointer. Sleeping on the UI thread is not a responsiveness solution.

sources.title: pywin32 client source
sources.summary: Primary implementation distinguishes GetActiveObject, Dispatch and DispatchEx. DispatchEx creates via CoCreateInstanceEx. Verify instance ownership rather than relying on generic Dispatch.
